spec.title: PROP-071: Change origin bindings and project-owned closure

p.NATIVE-ORIGIN-FIXTURE: A reusable feat declares native addressable facts and their explicit artifact requirements using PROP-043. Its intent is independent of a programming stack. A fixture binding selects an exact package coordinate/version together with exact fact addresses and captured authored manifest/document byte identities. The observed fact address and the versioned package selection are distinct; versionless fact metadata does not mean newest-slot authority. Leaf digests in this fixture establish byte identity, not original-package authentication.

p.ORIGIN-LOCAL-IDENTITY: Two consuming projects may reference the same immutable origin while authoring different local refinement and acceptance facts. Package fact addresses retain the package coordinate; local addresses retain their own project coordinate. A reference never copies package status into local authority. Consumer-owned materialization may add derived records but may not modify the authored package leaf bytes.

p.BINDING-OBSERVATION-FIXTURE: The initial change fixtures use the incumbent declared fact observation and requirements metadata query, retaining exact package/local addresses, authored artifact sets and separate authoring/adoption observations. Test-only fixture metadata does not commission a durable change parser, a closure evaluator or publication machinery. Fixture evidence may land before those later owners.

p.LOCAL-ACCEPTANCE-NOT-INHERITED: A package's authored done status, an absent or recorded adoption observation, and a copied status marker do not satisfy a selected local acceptance obligation. A copied paragraph, if valid local markup, is observed at its own local address; it does not replace a different selected local fact. Missing selected acceptance stays missing. Even a local done marker is not terminal proof by itself: PROP-043's declared artifact obligations and independent evidence remain separate. The metadata query reports no portable terminal verdict, and these fixture tests must not claim an acceptance runtime exists.

p.BINDING-PLANNING-INDEPENDENCE: Shared change intent and origin/local selections contain no personal owner/current/done scheduler state. Fixture personal-plan and work-coverage bytes are separate observations; editing them cannot rewrite shared binding, authored local obligations or immutable origin bytes. An adoption registry observation may change while shared intent stays unchanged. No second cursor or scheduler is created by observing these axes.

p.BINDING-TERMINAL-EVIDENCE-AXES: The incumbent terminal resolver receives the exact addressed fact's authored marker/requirements and an independently typed evidence-provider observation. Work coverage, adoption, authoring status and terminal artifacts are distinct. A work edge or personal done flag cannot replace missing or unavailable implementing evidence. Valid existing artifacts may be observed without fabricating a work item. Fixture checks use the existing terminal API and retain per-artifact states/locators, without promoting the requirements metadata report into a portable acceptance runtime. The initial fixture work observation is separate personal-plan data and an unattributed legacy refs bag; it defines no typed Work artifact or new registered relation.

p.CHANGE-DIRECTORY-IDENTITY: Epoch-one change IDs are exactly chg- followed by32lowercase hexadecimal digits. The immutable node-relative home is configured-spec-root/changes/id/change.toml; no slug or title enters that directory or a document address. A trusted host supplies a validated project-relative configured spec root, defaulting to the incumbent current layout root. The manifest cannot grant a different root. This parser-level configuration is not a newly implemented project-settings or CLI override.

p.CHANGE-AUTHORED-GRAMMAR: The authored TOML schema1 root contains change identity/selected-node/slug/title, exact qualified origin package pins with captured manifest/document SHA256 declarations and spec fact citations, explicit document rows, and an optional opaque metadata table for user values. Captures are declarations of selected byte identity, not authentication by editable hashes. The selected node must agree with actual trusted consumer context. Unknown epochs, malformed identity/origin and duplicate IDs refuse in the shared core owner before any application.

p.CHANGE-DOCUMENT-ROLES: The closed roles are intent, refinement, acceptance, work and closure. Role paths are portable literal paths relative to the immutable change directory and must be unique. Intent/refinement/acceptance may be normative authored inputs; work is authored but not normative intent; closure is derived output and must be neither normative nor input. A role confers no source interpretation or artifact truth. A closure path cannot alias another input role or become its own proof subject.

p.CHANGE-MIGRATION-REPLAY: The explicit pilot epoch0 to epoch1 recipe changes only the schema integer token after shared identity/path/role validation. Pilot0 is a frozen change fixture profile, not a claim that former prototype bindings were durable epoch0 manifests. Unknown source/target/recipe refuses; no implicit migration or file write occurs. The change planner reuses M13's exact ordered/non-overlap/original-token replay primitive and revalidates target text. Every untouched byte, comment and opaque user value survives; current epoch1 identity migration is byte-identical. A parser or proposal grants no filesystem application authority.

identities.title: 4. Independent authored intent and structural work

p.CHANGE-WORK-DAG: A declared input work-role document has its own closed TOML schema1: items with work- plus a lowercase ASCII letter followed by up to58 lowercase letters/digits/hyphens, predecessor IDs, artifact needs (kind and target declaration), and portable relative touches hints. Need kinds are specification, implementation, verification, documentation, decision, research, plan, disposition and external; targets are nonblank bounded literal declarations, not verified artifacts. IDs are unique across work documents; predecessor IDs must exist, and cycles, duplicate edges/needs/touches and unknown fields including done/owner/current refuse. The graph returns authored predecessors/needs/hints only, never completion, ready-to-run or scheduling verdicts.

p.CHANGE-INDEPENDENT-IDENTITIES: Intent recipe sha256:vibe-change-intent-v1 frames schema, immutable change ID, trusted consumer coordinate and selected node, sorted exact origin pins/capture declarations/document citations, and sorted normative role/path/exact retained bytes. Title/slug, opaque metadata, non-normative work, derived closure, observations and run logs are excluded. Exact authored normative bytes are the content boundary: this recipe makes no cross-format or whitespace semantic equivalence claim and authenticates no origin. Missing, extra or duplicate normative observations refuse instead of minting partial intent identity.

p.CHANGE-WORK-IDENTITY-FRAMING: Work recipe sha256:vibe-change-work-v1 binds the same immutable consumer/change scope and sorts items by ID, predecessors and touches lexically, and needs by lexical kind/target; authored ordering does not change graph identity. Distinct selected-contribution recipe sha256:vibe-change-work-contribution-v1 frames sorted selected IDs and their complete predecessor closure, excluding unrelated items. These structural contributions may inform later execution requests but are not execution authority. Every recipe begins with its name plus NUL epoch=1 NUL and uses be64(label length), label bytes, be64(value length), value bytes, with collection counts and explicit item boundaries. Schema field values are be32 and collection count values are be64; text is UTF8, normative content is exact bytes. Intent and work domains are distinct; closure creation cannot rewrite the intent snapshot it names.

p.CHANGE-CAPTURED-ANALYSIS: Change analysis consumes the actual immutable client-scoped M16 disk-plus-buffer capture. Derive node context from its retained node manifest and trusted configured relative spec root, then reuse the shared change parser/roles and exact-byte identity owner. Every input/diagnostic retains resource, capture, version, digest and original-byte basis; optional partial/invalid syntax preserves raw bytes and explicit missing position. Different clients' dirty refinements remain isolated. Analysis never reopens disk, saves, fetches, installs or writes lock/closure. A raw byte identity is not authenticated origin or effect authority.

p.CHANGE-SAVED-PREPARATION: A future authored edit is prepared only from saved recaptured node/change/input witnesses and a separately composed finite M16 document-edit grant. Derived closure is not a writable normative input. Revalidate exact buffer versions, disk observations and subject inputs against an explicit fresh capture, then reuse the existing M16 participant barrier; no new editor/writer protocol is created. Dirty inputs, changed affected state, foreign capture or old dirty plan after save refuse before writes. This change adapter performs analysis/preparation only: it does not acknowledge/apply a barrier, save, execute work or publish closure. Registered cooperative and final-comparison/rename limitations remain those of PROP080.

p.CHANGE-RETAINED-ORIGIN: Accept a whole-package origin only by joining its exact authored package pin, selected_content_hash and manifest/document byte declarations to a retained M01 selected capture. The optional selected_content_hash uses the incumbent ContentHash grammar: absent legacy data remains parseable but unbound, a differing binding refuses, and absent retained bytes are separately unavailable. Initial binding is explicit: verify legacy pin/manifest/cited bytes against an actual retained capture, then prepare insertion of its selected content identity under saved-state controls; absence is never filled implicitly. Keep that memory-held immutable observation separate from the current mutable slot. Reinstall cannot replace historical accepted bytes; a same-version content change reports origin-drift. Serialized hashes cannot recover lost retention or choose newest SemVer. Declared hashes and local record agreement do not authenticate originals or promote proof strength. A transformed output without retained authored original bytes is an explicit original-unavailable gap, not authored-source SHA. Reports identify exact selected fact addresses and unavailable selections; this boundary does not certify arbitrary paginated fact completeness.

p.CHANGE-BOUND-INTENT: All-absent legacy origin bindings retain the exact sha256:vibe-change-intent-v1 framing and golden digests. Any present binding selects the distinct sha256:vibe-change-bound-intent-v1 domain in IntentIdentity. Its framing otherwise follows the legacy recipe, adding after each origin manifest an origin-content-present byte field (0 absent, 1 present), and for present bindings an origin-selected-content exact UTF8 hash field. Every origin's presence remains explicit: partial binding cannot make another origin accepted. Work/contribution recipes are unchanged. A content-only package update with unchanged cited leaves has an empty selected-fact delta but changes the authored selected binding and bound intent after explicit rebase. The new schema1 native parser reads old unbound syntax; an older deny-unknown parser refuses the new field. This is non-bidirectional compatibility, without a forced migration, registry epoch/window change or a new generated JSON contract.

p.CHANGE-EXPLICIT-REBASE: Rebase is an explicit reviewable proposal naming old and new retained captures and the affected addressed fact identities. Validate the new declarations through the shared change grammar and preserve unrelated authored bytes/comments. Bind the proposed new intent to saved captured change inputs and the existing finite M16 edit grant, buffer versions and fresh-capture barrier admission. Dirty, stale or missing retained origins refuse without writes; preparing rebase never installs, hydrates, automatically applies an edit, changes package slots or overwrites historical evidence. The cooperative publication boundary remains PROP080.
